plan: i want to do something ambitious. I want to have a ISO of this setup, so the setup should start directly when booted from the iso over for example an usb. get inspiration of omarchy https://github.com/omacom/omarchy the goal for now is a detailed plan.

turns.question: What should appear when someone boots the USB?
turns.recommendedAnswer: The configured Hyprland live desktop with an explicit Install launcher, so users can try the setup without touching their disks.
turns.userAnswer: Start the setup/installation wizard directly; no full live desktop
turns.notes: User selected installer-first rather than a live desktop. ISO session is an installation environment; configured Hyprland is the installed outcome.

turns.question: Who must the first release serve?
turns.recommendedAnswer: A public experimental release for technical users, with a narrow tested hardware matrix rather than a general-purpose distro promise.
turns.userAnswer: Public release for newcomers with a polished supported installation
turns.notes: Requires stronger onboarding, safety, support documentation, hardware validation, and release gates than the recommended technical preview.

turns.question: Which base should the ISO use?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Vanilla Arch Linux with archiso; the existing pacman/AUR package model fits it without inheriting another distro's custom repositories.
turns.userAnswer: Vanilla Arch Linux

turns.question: Which hardware must v1 explicitly support and test?
turns.recommendedAnswer: x86_64 Intel/AMD graphics plus a QEMU/KVM test target; treat NVIDIA as experimental unless it is essential to your machines.
turns.userAnswer: x86_64 PCs with Intel or AMD graphics; x86_64 PCs with NVIDIA graphics; Laptops with hybrid Intel/AMD plus NVIDIA graphics; QEMU/KVM virtual machines; VirtualBox or VMware virtual machines
turns.notes: Broad release matrix selected. Define NVIDIA generations and the actual hardware/VM release evidence in a dependent round. ARM64 not selected.

turns.question: What firmware compatibility is required?
turns.recommendedAnswer: UEFI with Secure Boot disabled for v1; legacy BIOS and Secure Boot signing add separate implementation and testing work.
turns.userAnswer: UEFI only; Secure Boot disabled

turns.question: What must work without internet?
turns.recommendedAnswer: The default desktop and default disk installation, if included, work offline; optional applications can require internet. This makes USB boot independent of mirrors and AUR availability.
turns.userAnswer: Offline default desktop/install; optional extras online
turns.notes: Applied to selected installer-only boot: ISO boots installer offline and installs a usable default desktop offline.

turns.question: How much of today's selectable setup should ship on the ISO?
turns.recommendedAnswer: One curated default profile generated from packages.json, preserving other choices for installation or later configuration rather than bundling everything.
turns.userAnswer: One representative default profile; keep optional choices available separately

turns.question: Should changes made while running from USB survive reboot?
turns.recommendedAnswer: A disposable live session in v1; persistent USB storage is a separate feature with filesystem and privacy implications.
turns.userAnswer: No persistence; every USB boot starts clean

turns.question: Which Omarchy ideas should guide this project?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Borrow installer structure, prebuilt package delivery, and release testing, while keeping this project's appearance and application choices.
turns.userAnswer: Prebuilt packages and offline installation; Polished onboarding and cohesive defaults
turns.notes: Omarchy is inspiration for these selected aspects, not authorization to fork it or adopt its appearance/update system.

turns.question: What should happen to the current setup-on-existing-Arch workflow?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Preserve it and share package/configuration logic with the ISO rather than replacing it.
turns.userAnswer: Other: the github repo is currently also an aur package. this should be kept. iso will be a release artifact on github releases.
turns.notes: Preserve AUR distribution and add ISO as a GitHub Release artifact. Need check current PKGBUILD and resolve compatibility requirements for existing workflows.

turns.question: How should v1 be built and distributed?
turns.recommendedAnswer: A documented local build plus manually approved experimental releases; introduce automated publication only after VM and hardware gates work.
turns.userAnswer: Automated CI builds and public releases from the start
turns.notes: Use GitHub Releases per preceding answer. Define publication gates, runner constraints, artifact splitting, and signing policy.

turns.question: What image-size constraint should the plan optimize for?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Target an 8 GB USB drive and measure actual ISO/RAM use before declaring hard limits.
turns.userAnswer: No initial size target; prioritize functionality
turns.notes: GitHub Release per-asset limits still constrain distribution and require evidence-backed handling.

turns.question: If the offline ISO exceeds GitHub's under-2-GiB per-asset limit, how should we distribute it?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Preserve offline functionality and use split GitHub assets with a documented verified reassembly helper; users must reassemble them before flashing.
turns.userAnswer: Other: both 1. and 2.
turns.notes: Refers to split GitHub Release assets with reassembly/verification tools AND a full externally hosted ISO linked from GitHub Releases. External hosting choice/availability remains to resolve.

turns.question: What should the automatically launched installer look like?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Extend the existing Rust TUI with a guided ISO mode; it works without a graphics driver and preserves the project's current interface.
turns.userAnswer: Guided text/terminal installer based on the existing Rust TUI

turns.question: Which disk-installation modes must v1 offer?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Erase one explicitly selected whole disk only, with a clear destructive-action summary and typed confirmation; dual boot and partition resizing multiply the risk.
turns.userAnswer: Erase disk or install into existing unallocated space; never resize
turns.notes: Requires existing-partition/ESP preservation, free-space validation, boot entry policy, multi-disk guardrails, and negative tests.

turns.question: Which installed filesystem/recovery policy should v1 use?
turns.recommendedAnswer: One fixed Btrfs layout with snapshots and a tested recovery path, building on the project's existing Timeshift/grub-btrfs integration rather than exposing many layouts.
turns.userAnswer: Btrfs with snapshots and a tested recovery path

turns.question: What encryption policy should the installer offer?
turns.recommendedAnswer: LUKS2 encryption enabled by default with an explicit opt-out and clear passphrase/recovery guidance; do not collect any actual passphrase here.
turns.userAnswer: Encryption optional and off by default

turns.question: How should ISO defaults relate to packages.json?
turns.recommendedAnswer: An explicit ISO profile with the same desktop identity, using redistributable prebuilt packages and audited substitutions where needed; keep AUR-install defaults unchanged.
turns.userAnswer: Allow an explicit ISO-specific default profile; preserve existing AUR defaults

turns.question: When should users choose and install optional online applications?
turns.recommendedAnswer: After the first successful desktop boot, keeping network/AUR failures out of the base OS installation.
turns.userAnswer: Inside the USB installer when internet is available
turns.notes: Keep offline base installation independent of optional online selections; clarify behavior if downloads fail.

turns.question: How should optional coding agents appear in the ISO experience?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Do not bundle agent binaries or run remote installers during base installation; offer them later through the existing optional agent selector with manual authentication.
turns.userAnswer: Offer coding agents later; no agent required for offline installation

turns.question: What implementation direction should the plan take for partitioning and base Arch installation?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Evaluate a pinned archinstall backend behind the Rust wizard, with an early offline/encryption proof before committing; avoid inventing a partitioning engine.
turns.userAnswer: Use pinned archinstall if an early integration proof passes
turns.notes: Spike must include install into unallocated space, ESP preservation, selected Btrfs recovery scheme, and optional LUKS2. Failure triggers an explicit new architecture decision, not silent fallback.

turns.question: Beyond keeping the AUR package, what compatibility must the plan preserve?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Keep the current command, existing-system setup, package choices, and config-preservation behavior; add a distinct ISO mode.
turns.userAnswer: Preserve current command and existing-system setup behavior

turns.question: How should v1 define NVIDIA support?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Support explicitly tested GPUs supported by current Arch drivers, including hybrid laptops; detect unsupported/legacy GPUs early instead of promising all NVIDIA generations.
turns.userAnswer: Current-driver-supported, explicitly tested NVIDIA and hybrid hardware
turns.notes: Potential conflict with later VM-only release gate; must reconcile tested hardware scope versus candidate support.

turns.question: How should public support claims be verified?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Automated VM gates plus recorded physical Intel/AMD, NVIDIA, and hybrid-laptop checks before a stable release; missing evidence blocks that support claim.
turns.userAnswer: Release after VM tests; label physical-hardware support unverified
turns.notes: Requires reconciliation with newcomer-facing supported release and explicitly tested NVIDIA selection. VM tests cannot establish physical GPU behavior.

turns.question: What build infrastructure can the plan rely on?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Start with GitHub-hosted runners and a pinned Arch build environment, measure resource limits, and make a dedicated runner a documented escalation rather than an assumption.
turns.userAnswer: GitHub-hosted runners only initially; assess limits in a build spike

turns.question: When should automation publish an ISO?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Tag-triggered builds with automatic prerelease publication after tests; stable promotion requires the selected hardware evidence, not publication on every commit.
turns.userAnswer: Tags publish stable releases automatically after automated tests

turns.question: What authenticity guarantees should releases provide?
turns.recommendedAnswer: SHA-256 checksums, a signed checksum manifest, and build provenance; checksums alone detect corruption but do not authenticate the publisher.
turns.userAnswer: Checksums only for v1
turns.notes: Record authenticity limitation; checksums detect corruption but are not publisher authentication.

turns.question: How should installed machines receive updates?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Normal Arch/AUR package updates plus explicit setup/config updates that preserve user edits; do not add a custom distro update service in v1.
turns.userAnswer: Normal Arch/AUR updates; explicit non-destructive setup/config updates

turns.question: What localization must v1 provide?
turns.recommendedAnswer: English installer text with explicit keyboard, timezone, and system-locale selection; remove hardcoded Swiss-German defaults from the ISO path.
turns.userAnswer: English and German UI; selectable system localization

turns.question: How should we reconcile broad NVIDIA/hybrid support with VM-only release gates?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Implement support for current drivers, publish stable tags after VM gates as requested, but label all physical GPU compatibility unverified until device-specific evidence exists.
turns.userAnswer: Target current physical GPUs, but explicitly label them unverified at release
turns.notes: Supersedes the explicitly-tested physical-hardware boundary from turn 23. Public newcomer-oriented stable releases are VM-validated, not physically hardware-certified.

turns.question: Which virtual machines must be release-tested automatically?
turns.recommendedAnswer: QEMU/KVM with UEFI and working 3D acceleration is mandatory; document VirtualBox/VMware as unverified until separately tested, since desktop graphics behavior differs.
turns.userAnswer: QEMU/KVM required; VirtualBox and VMware documented but unverified

turns.question: What external-hosting contract should the plan use for the full ISO?
turns.recommendedAnswer: User-provisioned S3-compatible object storage with a public HTTPS download URL and automated CI uploads; keep provider/bucket/credentials as deployment configuration, not source code or interview answers.
turns.userAnswer: Plan S3-compatible object storage and public HTTPS downloads
turns.notes: Provider-neutral S3 deployment contract. Provisioning endpoint/bucket/CI credentials is a future infrastructure prerequisite, not authorization to create paid infrastructure now.

turns.question: If one required distribution destination fails, what should release automation do?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Keep the GitHub release draft until GitHub parts and the full mirror ISO are uploaded and verified; retry uploads without rebuilding different bytes.
turns.userAnswer: Publish verified GitHub assets even if the mirror is temporarily unavailable
turns.notes: Mirror failure is non-blocking. Mark mirror unavailable, omit invalid URLs, retry publishing the exact same verified bytes.

turns.question: If an optional application cannot download or install, what should happen?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Preserve the completed offline base, show the failure clearly, and let the user retry or explicitly skip it; never report that application as installed.
turns.userAnswer: Keep the base installed; offer explicit Retry or Skip with a final summary

turns.question: What should 'install into unallocated space' guarantee?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Support existing Windows or Linux on GPT disks, never resize/format their partitions, preserve their EFI files/entries, and let firmware select the OS; a unified cross-OS GRUB menu is not required in v1.
turns.userAnswer: Preserve Windows/Linux and require a unified boot menu
turns.notes: Requires GRUB integration plus reliable identification and preservation of foreign boot targets. Unsupported layouts must be refused before writes; clarify supported foreign-OS boundary if needed.

turns.question: What must the tested Btrfs recovery path provide?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Initial/system snapshots plus a guided recovery mode on the ISO that restores the system and repairs matching boot files; leave personal files untouched and do not call snapshots a backup.
turns.userAnswer: Guided ISO-based snapshot restore and boot repair; no snapshot boot-menu requirement

turns.question: Which baseline should the plan specify?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Firefox, Fish, Kitty, Zellij, Neovim, Kate, Waybar, SwayNC, Wofi, Merkuro, Bluedevil, plasma-nm, and pavucontrol-qt; retain this project's Hyprland theme and keybindings, omit agents and a dock, and audit all bundled assets.
turns.userAnswer: Other: packages as recommended in 1. but instead of zejllji, use herdr.
turns.notes: Final profile uses Herdr instead of Zellij. Current package registry identifies herdr-bin as AUR. Audit redistribution, runtime dependencies, offline launch, and update path; do not silently substitute another multiplexer.

turns.question: Must v1 support hibernation to disk?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Normal shutdown and suspend only, with suspend explicitly hardware-dependent; defer hibernation because swap/resume setup interacts with encryption and Btrfs recovery.
turns.userAnswer: No hibernation guarantee in v1; shutdown and suspend only

turns.question: Which existing installations should the unified-menu promise cover?
turns.recommendedAnswer: GPT/UEFI Windows and Linux with discoverable, intact EFI loaders; reject unsupported or ambiguous layouts before writes, never resize partitions, and warn BitLocker users that boot changes can trigger recovery.
turns.userAnswer: Discoverable intact GPT/UEFI loaders only; refuse unsupported layouts before writes

turns.question: What Windows-specific evidence should block release?
turns.recommendedAnswer: Require synthetic Windows-style partition/EFI preservation tests and real Linux dual-boot VM tests, but label actual Windows/BitLocker boot unverified until a licensed test image is supplied. A fake EFI fixture must not be reported as a Windows boot test.
turns.userAnswer: Fixtures and Linux dual-boot gate releases; actual Windows/BitLocker boot remains explicitly unverified
turns.notes: Final user-facing release notes and installer warnings must distinguish implemented detection/chainloading from unverified actual Windows/BitLocker boot.
